close_reason: Already documented: helpers.rs:91-103 explains the byte-index check, names the three cases (messageId, messageId/0, messageIdX), and explains why starts_with alone would be wrong.
description: email.rs find_immutable_patch_key checks key.as_bytes().get(field.len()) == Some(&b'/') in addition to key == field. This distinguishes 'messageId' (blocked), 'messageId/0' (blocked, sub-path), and 'messageIdX' (allowed, unrelated field with shared prefix). A naive starts_with(field) refactor would silently block legitimate fields that share a prefix with an immutable field name. The byte-index check is load-bearing — do not simplify it.
title: find_immutable_patch_key uses byte-index check not starts_with to guard patch paths
